Covering estimates and Haar normalization then give the exact measure inequality, including dimension zero. This agrees with [Simon, Theorem 2.10](https://web.stanford.edu/class/math285/ts-gmt.pdf) and supplies the normalization needed by good_points.

Finite total mass justifies the unit-dual-norm argument. The covering estimate establishes a finite-Hausdorff-measure carrier before Radon–Nikodym is applied. Removing zero/infinite-density and nonunit points gives the stated pointwise conditions, while normalization and change of density preserve the current representation.

The covering-tail argument and isodiametric_bound yield the sharp upper-density constant 1. The field bound supplies integrability for Besicovitch differentiation. Multiplying the vanishing average error by the bounded density ratio proves exactly the stated ENNReal operator-norm limit.

The good-point estimates give both carrier-density bounds and vanishing rescaled error. CT supplies the subsequence and measure inequalities; const_mass and the comparison estimate establish the mass conclusions. Dilation invariance and the explicit SLIM hypothesis establish ISP of the limit. All concentration, compact-finiteness and convergence conclusions are accounted for.

The distributional boundary identity gives translation invariance. Coordinate expansion and growth force the invariant subspace to have dimension d+1 and the vector to be simple. Haar decomposition and lower density give atoms of weight at least c; growth bounds their total weight and number. Positivity near the origin supplies the zero offset.

The proof uses only the stated REP, SL and CT hypotheses. The empty-annulus argument produces slices with vanishing boundary mass; projection, density representation and the supplied BV estimate give L¹ convergence. Measurable hulls handle arbitrary, potentially nonmeasurable N_k. Lipschitz measure comparison and the compact-set limsup bound then imply every weight is at least one.

The coordinate calculation proves that C is a cycle and computes its half-space slice boundaries. SL makes ISP applicable to actual slice currents. const_mass and MR identify their mass measures, forcing the positive coefficient to equal a natural-valued multiplicity on a set of positive measure. The d = 0 slice is explicitly covered.

All four declared dependencies apply with the stated hypotheses. LD supplies the lower density for constant_planes; weight_ge_one collapses the measure to a single unit-weight plane; plane_integer gives integrality. The determinant argument identifies the plane independently of the subsequence, and the subsequence criterion proves the exact approximate-tangent predicate.

The proof establishes a.e. strong measurability of the chosen plane projections through quadratic moments, then applies the explicit RECT hypothesis. It selects a Borel full-measure carrier, proves tangent invariance under the null modification, and verifies every IMRep field and the representation identity. No unstated IMC hypothesis or parent conclusion is used.
